definition_title: Krull dimension under going-up and finite normalization
natural_language_statement: A surjective order map with the stated chain-lifting property cannot increase order Krull dimension. An injective integral ring homomorphism preserves ring Krull dimension. Consequently, a finite-type algebra R over a field k admits an injective finite k-algebra homomorphism from a polynomial ring in s variables, with ring Krull dimension of R equal to s.
explanation: The chain-lifting theorem preserves the length and last element of a finite strict chain, yielding the Krull-dimension inequality. Integral extensions give the reverse dimension comparison through lying-over and going-up; finite normalization then identifies the dimension of a finite-type algebra with the number of polynomial generators in the normalization.
